sections.heading: You Wanted a Second Opinion, Not a Sales Pitch
body: A shingle lifts in the wind, or a brown ring spreads across the ceiling, and the question is whether it's a repair or a new roof. You can't climb up and check for yourself, so you end up trusting whoever sounds the most sure.
That's a lot to hand a stranger. Before any quote, you want someone who will look and tell you what's really going on.

sections.heading: What Customers Mention About Dusty's Visits
body: Reviewers describe much the same visit: Dusty looks at the roof, explains it in plain words and answers their questions. His name comes up in review after review.
Dusty Rieck owns Sandhill Roofing. Here is what customers mention, in their own reviews:
list: The roof looked at and explained in plain words
Questions answered, with no pressure to buy
Samples and options to choose from
A free roof replacement estimate, which Sandhill's own site offers

sections.heading: Finally, a Straight Answer From Someone Who Knows Roofs
body: A roof call usually starts with a question you can't answer on your own: what do I have, and what does it need? One new homeowner described what happened when they called around.

sections.quote: As a new home owner I called 15 different roofing companies and 7 different shingle suppliers to figure out what type of roof I had. Dusty answered my call and immediately gave me proper guidance, knowledge, and went over the top to help me figure out my issue.
sections.name: Joe B.

sections.heading: Not Sure It's the Roof? Describe What You're Seeing
body: Shingles missing after a windy day, a stain or drip on the ceiling, granules in the gutters, dents after hail: whatever you're seeing, call (402) 890-6460 and describe it.

sections.quote: Dusty came out and looked at a leak in our ceiling that we assumed was due to a roof issue. … Although the issue wasn't with the roof, he knew exactly where it was and who we should contact …
sections.name: Darion M.

sections.heading: Years Later, Customers Still Call Dusty
body: Reviewers mention getting in touch with Dusty after the job was done, in one case nine years after the roof went on.

sections.quote: I contacted Dusty to ask for documentation about a roof that he installed nine years ago. … He promptly and cheerfully provided the info. Our customers were happy with the roof Dusty installed and were very pleased that he continues to provide excellent service years later!
sections.name: Nicole S.

sections.heading: Roofing, Siding, Gutters, Windows and Doors
sections.intro: One call covers your roof and the rest of the outside of your house.

sections.heading: Storm Damage and Your Insurance Company
body: After hail or wind, the roof is only half of it. The other half is the claim, and we handle insurance claims.
We can't tell you what your insurer will decide, and your agent is the one to ask about your policy and your deductible.

sections.heading: Roof Replacement: When the Roof Has Run Its Course
body: When a roof is worn out or storm-damaged, replacement is the job. Our materials list covers asphalt, steel, stone coated steel, standing seam steel, rubber slate, polymer and cedar shake, along with impact resistance. Call for the free roof replacement estimate.

sections.heading: Selling a House With a Roof That Needs Work?
body: Several reviewers had a closing date to meet, as the seller or as the agent for one. If that's you, tell us the date when you call.

sections.quote: I had to get a new roof put on a property I was selling in order to close by a certain date. Dusty got the job done in the small window of nice weather and did a great job.
sections.name: Steve G.

We're based in Lincoln and serve Eastern Nebraska. Give us your address when you call, and we'll tell you whether we can get to you.

sections.heading: Questions to Bring to Any Estimate
body: Whichever roofer you call, ask what the estimate covers. A number with no detail behind it is hard to compare.

items.title: Size and pitch
items.text: Ask how big the roof is and how steep, and whether the estimate says so.

items.title: Material
items.text: The estimate should name the material you're getting.

items.title: What comes off first
items.text: Ask how many layers of old roofing there are and what happens if wood underneath has to be replaced.

items.title: The details
items.text: Ask whether chimneys, vents, valleys and flashing are included.

items.title: Cleanup
items.text: Ask how the crew handles the old shingles and nails.

sections.heading: What Lincoln Homeowners Ask About a New Roof

items.q: How much does a roof replacement cost?
items.a: It depends on the size and pitch of the roof, the material, how many layers come off and what the wood underneath needs. A number given without seeing the roof is a guess, so the free estimate is where you get the real figure.

items.q: How do I know whether I need a replacement or a repair?
items.a: Call (402) 890-6460 and describe what you see. If it's more than one spot on the roof, say so.

items.q: Will insurance pay for a new roof?
items.a: That depends on your policy, your deductible and what caused the damage. Your agent can answer it, and we handle insurance claims.

items.q: Will I get a sales pitch with the estimate?
items.a: Call (402) 890-6460, say what the roof is doing, and ask for the free estimate.

sections.heading: Get Your Roof Replacement Estimate
sections.text: Tell us how old the roof is and what you're seeing, and ask for the free roof replacement estimate at (402) 890-6460.

footer.about: Sandhill Roofing is a family-owned roofing company based in Lincoln, serving Eastern Nebraska. We handle roofing, siding, gutters, windows and doors, and insurance claims.
why: Roofing, siding, gutters, windows and doors

Your customers already make your case. 101 people have reviewed Sandhill Roofing on Google, and one thing keeps coming up: Dusty tells you what the roof needs and what it doesn't. mike B. wrote that he "didn't make me feel pressured or try to sell me on things that I didn't need."

Your website shows none of it. It's one homepage of about 362 words with no headline Google can read, no reviews, and a services page whose headings are your phone number, five times over. No headline says roofer, or Lincoln.
So we built a site that opens with roofer in Lincoln, NE, leads with the straight answer your customers describe, and gives roof replacement a page of its own.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Roofer People Find on Google in Lincoln
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page of the demo: what your site does today, and what we changed.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads first to learn what you do and where you work.
problems: Your homepage has no headline at all, so nothing tells Google you're a roofer in Lincoln.
None of your Google reviews appear on the site, so a visitor never sees what your customers say.
fixes: A headline that says roofer in Lincoln, NE, right at the top.
Your customers' own words, each beside the point it proves.

cards.title: Roof Replacement
cards.why: A new roof is a big decision, and today it has no page of its own.
problems: Roofing is one section of a separate services page with no address of its own, so a search for roof replacement in Lincoln has nothing to land on.
That page repeats its "When To Replace Your Roof" heading three times, which makes it look unfinished.
fixes: A full page for roof replacement in Lincoln, NE: repair or replacement, materials, the estimate and the job.
Your customers' stories beside each point.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn't think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a ready customer reaches you.
problems: Your contact page has no headline, and on a desktop screen your phone number is plain text, not a tap or click.
The form requires a street address and an "I'm not a robot" box, which is a lot to ask of someone with a leak.
fixes: Your number as the first button, with your hours and your email on the same page.
A short list of what to tell us when you call.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already describe the roofer you are. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame, and we'll walk you through this demo and what a full build adds.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your site shows no street address, while your Google listing puts you at 8120 Trendwood Dr, Lincoln, NE 68506, so which address should every listing use?
Your site headlines a lifetime workmanship warranty on roofing, siding and gutters but doesn't say what it covers, so what are the terms we should show?
Your site says you serve Eastern Nebraska without naming a town, while your reviews mention a property in Henderson and a home much closer to Omaha, so which towns should every listing name?

lead.heading: Why we led with the straight answer
lead.text: The scariest moment for a Lincoln homeowner is a roofer's quote for a whole new roof, and not knowing whether it's true. Your reviews are full of customers describing the opposite, a straight answer on what the roof needs and what it doesn't, and none of the competitor sites we could read says anything like it. That gives Google and AI tools something no generic roofing page has: your real reviews and your way of working.
